id.description: Unique identifier of the alert action.

createTimestamp.description: Time at which the alert action was created.

enabled.description: Denotes if the alert rule action is enabled or not being applied.

BrivoActionSettings.description: Settings for using a Brivo access point by an alert action. Supports Acctivation, Setting an Override and removing an override

service.description: Which service to use, has to be one of accessPoint, doorOverride, or doorOverrideCancel. There is accessPoint used to activate a brivo accesspoint. doorOverride is used to keep an access point activated either to a specified time or indefinite time. doorOverrideCancel removes the door override.

oauthId.description: The oauth id is the value that should be used to retrieve the oauth information from the oauth mode. These values are like access_token.

accessPointId.description: The access point id. It is a unique Id generated by Brivo. When serializer is used the access_point_name will be used to get this value.

BrivoOverRideSettings.description: Optional Field for adding an override values to the access point. Should only be used if adding an override value

endTimeMode.description:
When should over ride go to.
  UNTIL_TIME: Used to say when time ends. EndTime is required for this. Not providing this will raise an validation error.
  UNTIL_NEXT_SCHEDULE_CHANGE: Override will be placed until scheudle change is up
  INDEFINITE: Door override will be in place until forcibly removed.

behavior.description: With Override in place should access point be LOCKED or UNLOCK

endTime.description: The time format is iso-8601. This is used for when will the override be removed. This is not required if the endTimeMode is INDEFINITE

EbusActionSettings.description: Settings for sending an alert to EBUS.

url.description: The ip address or domain name of the mail server are both acceptable.

username.description: Check with ebus if this is required.

password.description: Check with ebus if this is required.

EvalinkTalosActionSettings.description: Settings for sending an alert via a Evalink Talos.  Currently only POST is supported.

auth_token.description: Optional bearer token to be included in the Authorization header when sending the the alert to Evalink Talos.

ImmixActionSettings.description: Settings for sending an Immix alert.

email.description: The email address where alert will be delivered.

url.description: Accepts either the IP address or domain name of the mail server.

port.description: The port number used to connect to the mail server.

username.description: Check with your monitoring service if this is required.

password.description: Check with your monitoring service if this is required.

tls.description: If TLS is not present in the settings, the default is false

NotificationActionSettings.description: Settings for sending notifications to a list of users.  Each item in the list is the id of the user and if the user wants email, push, and/or webapp notifications sent.

users.description: List of users to notify. Use `['*']` as the single item to target all users in the account.

id.description: Unique id of the user to notify. Use `'*'` to target all users in the account.

push.description: If true, try to notify the user using mobile push notifications.

email.description: If true, try to notify the user using email notifications.

webapp.description: If true, try to notify the user using an in-webapp popup notification. Webapp is a first-class channel — a user may opt into webapp only (with `email` and `push` both `false`). Omitting this field is equivalent to `false`.

rearmSeconds.description: If rearmSeconds are set, any alert that occurs for the alertActionRule within the rearmSeconds period will not be sent via email, push, and/or webapp. Instead, it will appear in /api/v3.0/notifications with the `status` = `throttled`

maxPerHour.description: If maxPerHour is set, for any alert that occurs for the alertActionRule over the maxPerHour in the last 60 minutes will not be sent via email, push, and/or webapp.  Instead,  it will appear in /api/v3.0/notifications with the `status` = `throttled`

OutputPortActionSettings.description: Settings for activating an output port alert action when an alert is triggered.

deviceId.description: The device id of the device to which the output port belongs.

duration.description: The duration in seconds for which the device output port should be activated.

portId.description: The device output port id to be activated.

PlaySpeakerAudioClipActionSettings.description:
Settings that determine where an audio clip is played when an alert is triggered.

The clip will be played on the union of:
- A fixed list of explicitly defined devices (`devices__in`), and
 - Optionally, additional triggering devices as defined by `playOnTriggeringDevice`:
  - **none**: Do not include any triggering device.
  - **alertActorDevices**: Include the device for which the event was created and from which the alert was generated.
  - **conditionRuleDevices**: Include the devices that the rule, which created the alert, is filtering on.

speakerAudioClipId.description: The ID of speaker audio clip to play.

playOnTriggeringDevice.description:
Specifies which devices should play the audio clip when the rule is triggered.
 - `none`: Do not attempt to play audio clips on any devices.
 - `alertActorDevices`: The device for which the event was created and from which the alert was triggered.
 - `conditionRuleDevices`: The devices that the rule, which created the alert, is filtering on.

devices__in.description:
A list of devices that will always play the audio clip,  
regardless of the device that triggered the alert.  
Format: `"<device_type>:<device_esn>"` (e.g., `"camera:10001abcd"`, `"speaker:1001abce"`)

SentinelActionSettings.description: Settings for sending an alert via a sentinel.  Currently only POST is supported.

auth_token.description: Optional bearer token to be included in the Authorization header when sending the the alert to Sentinel.

SlackActionSettings.description: Settings for sending an alert message to Slack.  Slack bot apps require the `chat:write` permissions scope. In addition, the bot app will need explicit permission to the channel selected in the settings via the Slack app.

apiToken.description: The Slack apiToken generated for your bot app.

channel.description: The Slack channel for sending alert messages.

SmsActionSettings.description: Settings for sending SMS notifications to a list of users. Each item in the list is the id of the user to notify via SMS.

users.description: List of users to notify via SMS. Use `['*']` as the single item to target all users in the account.

id.description: Unique id of the user to notify via SMS. Use `'*'` to target all users in the account.

SmtpActionSettings.description: Settings for sending an alert via SMTP.  This alert action is primarily used for monitoring services.

url.description: The ip address or domain name of the mail server are both acceptable.

username.description: Check with your monitoring service if this is required.

password.description: Check with your monitoring service if this is required.

tls.description: If tls is not present in the settings, the default is false

WebhookActionSettings.description: Settings for sending an alert via a webhook.  Currently only POST is supported.

auth_token.description: Optional bearer token to be included in the Authorization header when sending the alert to the webhook.

ZapierActionSettings.description: Settings for sending an alert via Zapier.  Currently only POST is supported.

url.description: The URL for the Zapier webhook to which alerts will be sent. This URL is provided by Zapier. For more information, refer to [Zapier Webhooks](https://help.zapier.com/hc/en-us/articles/8496083355661-How-to-Get-Started-with-Webhooks-by-Zapier#h_01HQ87H8BTMK49GY2RC8C4T59J) and [Trigger Zaps from Webhooks](https://help.zapier.com/hc/en-us/articles/8496288690317-Trigger-Zaps-from-webhooks#h_01HBGES5DW79VEMREX2Z7A0K48).

ZendeskActionSettings.description: Settings for sending an alert message to Zendesk and creating a ticket.

apiToken.description: The API token generated for your Zendesk account. For instructions on how to generate this token, please refer to [this guide](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408889192858-Managing-access-to-the-Zendesk-API#topic_bsw_lfg_mmb).

email.description: The email address associated with your Zendesk account. Please note that this email address does not need to be necessarily tied to a specific user and could belong to any admin or agent. Consider creating a dedicated user for automated interactions to streamline alert management.

subdomain.description: The subdomain associated with your Zendesk account. This should follow the format https://subdomain.zendesk.com. Please provide only the subdomain and not the full URL. For more information on finding your Zendesk subdomain, please refer to [this guide](https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4409381383578-Where-can-I-find-my-Zendesk-subdomain).

apiKey.description: The apiKey for your Zulip bot

email.description: The email address for your Zulip bot

organizationUrl.description: The url for your Zulip instance

allOf.description: Settings for sending a private alert message to a user Zulip. Zulip bots need to be supported by your organization. Bots can be created under `Personal Settings > Bots`.

user.description: The user's Zulip email or user number.

allOf.description: Settings for sending an alert message to a stream in Zulip. Zulip bots need to be supported by your organization. Bots can be created under `Personal Settings > Bots`.

stream.description: The name or id of a stream.

topic.description: The topic to post the message in.
